values.note: Campspot, one night for 2 adults before tax: Close to Water/No Services $32, Close to Water Electric & Water $34, Waterfront/No Services $36, Waterfront Electric & Water $38; the same on a Tuesday and a Saturday in October 2026. Plus the park's $2 'Booking Fee' once per stay and Campspot's own booking fee ($3 on these). The operator's page lists $32, $34 and $36 and a $28 budget site; Basic Site is capped at 20 ft and doesn't offer a motorhome type. Extra guest 14 or older $5 a night. 2027 isn't open for booking yet.

fees.source: https://www.campspot.com/park/seboomook-wilderness-campground (availability + per-type quotes 2026-10-17, 2026-10-20; 2027-06-08 and 2027-06-15 return nothing) + https://seboomookwildernesscampground.com/policies-pricing/ ('Nightly Base Rate (occupancy - 2)'), read 2026-11-02

values.note: Check-in 2 pm, check-out 11 am. Campsite cancellations up to 15 days out are refunded less $25; 7-14 days a credit less $25; 6 days or less nothing. No refunds or credits on holiday weekends or moose hunt weeks.

hookups.source: https://www.campspot.com/park/seboomook-wilderness-campground (site types 'Waterfront Site with Electric and Water', 'Close to water Electric & Water': 30-Amp, Water Hook-Up) + https://seboomookwildernesscampground.com/camping/ ('Electricity is available ONLY during Generator Hours of operation'), read 2026-11-02

values.note: Campspot lists 26 sites for a motorhome: 16 waterfront with electric and water, 6 waterfront without services (to 30 ft), 4 close to water (to 45 ft). Seven Basic sites are capped at 20 ft. Seasonal sites are also offered.

sites.source: https://seboomookwildernesscampground.com/ ('45 of them to be exact') + https://www.campspot.com/park/seboomook-wilderness-campground (types, sites, longest rig, rig types), read 2026-11-02

values.note: Wi-Fi only near the store, and only when the store is open and the electricity on ('WIFI does not broadcast to the campsites'). Dump station plus pump service at your site for an extra fee.

note: Private campground on the northwest shore of Moosehead Lake, at the end of 33 miles of dirt logging road: the operator says no 4WD is needed and rigs of every size come in, but warns off GPS (no signal once on the dirt, directions on its site) and asks you to yield to logging trucks. Electricity comes from a generator and runs only during its hours; guests' own generators off by 9 pm. --Claude
summary: Confirmed Campspot $32-38 base (motorhome types), 45 sites, 30A generator power, water at waterfront sites, showers, flush toilets, dump, store. Added 45-ft longest rig, pull-through, wifi with caveat. Road is 33 miles, not ~30; note updated. 2027 not bookable yet, so the rates are 2026's.

ACCESS: operator: 'Every kind of vehicle ... comes down the dirt road ... There are no washouts and no areas where 4-wheel drive is a necessity'; 33 miles of dirt, no gate fees via Greenville/Rockwood. A Google review from about a year ago, as far as I read: 'the road is no joke to get here. Make sure your tires and spares are ready ... don't drive over 30/35 mph - there's a lot of loose shale that will slice a tire to shreds'. No 4WD statement, so no criteria flag; it's a caveat for tires.

SEASONAL: operator home page: 'Seasonal camping sites are available! Come join our seasonal community!', no count. Campspot sells 33 of the 45 sites by the night including the 7 Basic. Imagery shows a clutch of RVs on a separate strip west of the store, which may be the seasonals; I can't tell from overhead. I read this as a nightly campground, not mostly seasonal.

WATERFRONT lakefront stands. Operator: 'sites right on the sandy shoreline', 'each ... has an Adirondack Lean-To that faces the open waters'; Campspot types 'Waterfront Site', and they're offered to a Class C. Imagery shows a road running behind the shore with small pads between it and the water on the south-east frontage; those pads are water-side of the road, so the road doesn't block them. Couldn't measure each pad.
